The thing is, I didn’t know I could actually travel and work at the same time. Years later, I quit my job to travel full-time because I DIDN’T KNOW these two things could co-exist. Then I met a digital nomad, and my view of life completely changed.

Don’t let anyone tell you that you can’t have both! You can, and if you want them, you have to go for it because regrets are what hurt the most! ✨

snippet.title: EPIC 12 things to do in Santa Marta - The Caribbean of Colombia!
snippet.description:
Let's talk about the EPIC 12 things to do in Santa Marta - the Caribbean of Colombia - a lively town in the Caribbean region of Magdalena, kissed by the biggest coastal mountain in the world, the Sierra Nevada de Santa Marta, and the most beautiful national park Colombia has to offer, Tayrona National Park 🐯 

Santa Marta is the perfect alternative to the bustling and bustling Cartagena, only a couple of hours away. The thing is, Santa Marta is the perfect destination for outdoorsy travelers and adventure seekers. Santa Marta is not only the oldest town in Colombia, but it also has such a laid-back vibe, perfect for days of chilling on its beaches, tons of waterfalls to jump into, hikes to explore, and viewpoints to admire ⛰️ 

I had the pleasure of spending a month in Santa Marta, and today I want to share the top 12 things to do here and why you definitely should have it on your Colombia itinerary! 🇨🇴

If you are treating your German job search like a UK or US application process, you are missing out on thousands of open roles. Filtering job boards for “Visa Sponsorship” is a massive mistake because the legal framework in Germany works completely differently.

The pressure isn’t on the employer to sponsor a highly restricted quota; the power is actually in your hands. When a company states they offer “relocation support,” that is your cue that they are friendly to international applicants.

Stop letting a lack of a “sponsorship” tag hold you back from applying. Focus on landing the offer first, and the visa logistics will follow.

snippet.title: Before You Move to Spain, Watch This #Spain #Moving #Expat
snippet.description:
Moving to Spain? Most people get at least one of these very wrong. First, your visa matters. The Spain Digital Nomad Visa needs approximately €2,300 per month, and you can't freely work locally. Second, the spain tax system is complex. You'll likely need a gestor or someone to handle tax and administrative tasks, and timing your move can cost you thousands. Third, spanish bureaucracy is slow. Getting your TIE or ID card can take months. Fourth, housing is competitive and often lacks heating or AC. Fifth, you'll need Spanish. Life admin without it is tough. Spain's lifestyle is incredible, but only if you're prepared. Get these right before you move. Learn more here: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=82HpoS3u2HI 👀
